name: Caillié to Timbuktu and across the Sahara
summary: A baker's son from Poitou, travelling alone and disguised as a Muslim returning to Egypt, walks from the Guinea coast to Djenné, takes a boat down the Niger to Timbuktu, and crosses the Sahara with a salt caravan to Morocco: the first European to come back from Timbuktu alive. He found a modest town of mud houses, not the city of gold Europe had imagined.

stops.note: Caillié sets out inland from the coast of Guinea.
Across the Fouta Djallon to the upper Niger.
Five months lying ill with scurvy and fever.
The great mosque city of the inland Niger delta.
Two weeks in the city: 'a mass of ill-looking houses built of earth'.
North with a caravan of six hundred camels.
Two months across the desert, half dead of thirst.
The French consul takes him in and ships him home.
